title: 電気回路Ⅰ（再履修クラス）
subtitle: Electric Circuit I
teachers:
FUKASAWA Toru
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of electric circuits consisting of resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and their combinations connected to an AC power source. In addition, students will learn about phasor representation of sinusoidal AC.
advice:
Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

AC circuit basics: properties of sine wave AC, effects of resistance, inductance, and capacitance, average and RMS values, phasor indication of sinusoidal AC

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit II, Electrical Circuit III, and Electrical Circuit IV), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a basic course requirement.
Based on the level of student understanding as indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. We encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don't understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can draw and explain the waveform of a sine wave alternating current.
Participants can formulate the circuit equations for AC circuits consisting of R, L, and C.
Participants can calculate average and rms values of sine wave AC.
Participants can represent the phasor of sine wave AC.

achievementLevels.ideal: Participants can correctly draw and sufficiently explain the waveform of a sine wave AC and be able to correctly formulate the circuit equations of a sine wave AC circuit consisting of R, L, and C. They can correctly calculate the average and RMS values of a sine wave AC and sufficiently explain the physical meaning of the RMS value. They can represent correctly the phasor of a sine wave AC and sufficiently explain why complex numbers are introduced in the calculation of sine wave AC circuits.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can draw and explain the waveform of a sine wave AC, and formulate the circuit equations of a sine wave AC circuit consisting of R, L, and C. They can calculate the average and RMS values of a sine wave AC and explain the physical meaning of the RMS value. They can represent the phasor of a sine wave AC and explain why complex numbers are introduced in the calculation of sine wave AC circuits.

              This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn the fundamentals of electric circuits consisting of resistance (R), inductance (L), capacitance (C), and their combinations connected to an AC power source. In addition, students will learn about phasor representation of sinusoidal AC.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

AC circuit basics: properties of sine wave AC, effects of resistance, inductance, and capacitance, average and RMS values, phasor indication of sinusoidal AC

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit II, Electrical Circuit III, and Electrical Circuit IV), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a basic course requirement.
Based on the level of student understanding as indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and course content.
